prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M. Out of scope: grid, port. Offshore Substation (Morrowick; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; Switching Window Acknowledgment); Main Transformer (site-specific trip; trends escalated); export cable→Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere; Export Limit Advisory→Grid Dispatcher if capability<target; applies Dispatcher ceiling); Grid Dispatcher: requirements→Relay. Turbine: Turbine Controller (Glassfin; validated commands; Pitch Deviation Notice; safe mode on aux loss; shutdown on confirmed fire), Pitch System (blades safe on emergency shutdown), Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet (isolated on fire/overheat), Nacelle Condition Monitor (fault vs fire), Turbine Sensor Bus. Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur; Leading Edge Tile Image). Substation: Export Cable Monitor (alarms→Control Engineer), Fire Detection Panel (supervised; located alarms), Emergency Generator (Foxglove; auto start on aux loss; load priorities; no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace→Substation Operator), Helideck. Modes: Substation Degraded, Grid Constraint, Weather Hold, Vessel Standby, Turbine Lockout (no remote restart during fire investigation). Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard). Alarms: safety>protection>export; not cleared on detector reset. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale; timestamped data→Shore Control Room; Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway). Shore Control Room (Amber Quay; hub; holds last limit on grid comms loss). Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown; Squall Window Bulletin; Deferred Task Rationale). Operations Radio Console (voice to CTV, SOV, Daughter Craft). Personnel Tracking Console. Weather Analyst: Wave Burst Record; Visibility Confidence Note→Duty Planner. Marine Coordinator: Berth Slot Confirmation. Vessel Master: read-back; Transfer Manifest Addendum; Crew Count Correction→Personnel Tracking Console. Recovery Basket Load Sheet→Rescue Coordinator. HSE Officer: exposure/evacuation advice; uses entry history for accountability. Field Supervisor: work status→Shore Control Room; reviews denial patterns/exceptions. Control Engineer verifies protection; Electrical Technician inspects only when isolated. North Access Scanner: person presents credential; checks authorization active for work period and area in scope; expired/suspended/incomplete→deny; gate stays secured if unverifiable; denial→contact Field Supervisor/HSE Officer; no verbal/image override; entry only if all checks pass; each attempt unique transaction ID

New part:
S839: Each entrant presents an individually assigned credential for validation.
S840: The scanner checks that the credential is active and belongs to the person presenting it.
S841: Access is granted only when the person has current authorization for the requested area and time.
S842: The route does not provide an alternate way to bypass work authorization or site restrictions.
S843: The scanner records each successful entry and each denied attempt with a time reference.
S844: The record supports routine review of access activity and investigation of anomalies.
S845: A local visual indicator communicates whether entry is permitted or denied.
S846: The entry barrier remains closed when validation fails or the scanner cannot complete a check.
S847: Personnel must not hold the barrier open for another entrant.
S848: Anti-tailgating measures are applied at the southern entry point.
S849: Visitors and temporary personnel follow the same identity checks as other entrants.
S850: Any escort requirement is verified before access is granted.
S851: The route is kept physically separated from areas that are not authorized for general access.
S852: Signs identify the permitted approach and direct personnel to the controlled entry point.
S853: The installation team verifies the scanner, barrier, and communications before the route is placed in service.
S854: Routine checks confirm that credential readers, indicators, and barrier controls operate as intended.
S855: Faults are reported promptly, and the route is placed out of service if secure operation cannot be assured.
S856: When the scanner is unavailable, personnel use an approved alternative entry process rather than an uncontrolled bypass.
S857: Emergency egress remains available without requiring an access credential from the inside of the route.
S858: Changes to the southern route are reviewed under the same change-control process as other access rules.
S859: East Service Lift runs a door-interlock and overload check before accepting a movement request.
S860: The Field Supervisor coordinates the inspection before the first planned movement of each operating shift.
S861: The inspection begins with a visual check of the car, landing doors, guide surfaces, and access barriers.
S862: The inspector confirms that the car floor and landing thresholds are clear of loose material and standing water.
S863: Door interlocks are tested at each served landing to confirm that the car cannot move while a door is open.
S864: The emergency stop and alarm are tested using the approved functional test procedure.
S865: The inspector checks the operating controls for damage, legibility, and secure mounting.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
